lesson.title: Rationales for Imperialism from 1750 to 1900
lesson.summary: How economic motives, nationalism, religious missions, and ideas such as Social Darwinism and the civilizing mission were used to justify empire.
learningGoals: Explain how ideologies contributed to the development of imperialism from 1750 to 1900.
Distinguish economic motives from ideological justifications for empire.
lesson.bigIdea: Industrial states built empires for economic and strategic reasons and justified them with ideas of racial and cultural superiority.
lesson.context: By the late 1800s, industrial powers had the motives and the means to expand. They also developed ideas that made conquest seem natural or even generous.

sections.title: Economic and national motives

blocks.text: Several forces drove imperialism in the 1800s. Factories needed raw materials such as cotton and rubber, and industrialists wanted new markets. Nationalism made colonies a matter of prestige: owning an empire showed that a nation was a great power.
Strategic needs mattered too. Steamships needed coaling stations, and navies needed bases around the world.

blocks.title: Cause and effect
blocks.text: Industrial demand for raw materials and markets, combined with national rivalry, pushed states to seek colonies.

sections.takeaway: Economic needs and national prestige drove imperial expansion.

sections.title: Justifying empire

blocks.text: Social Darwinism applied ideas of competition and survival of the fittest to human societies, claiming that stronger nations deserved to dominate. Scientists today reject this misuse of Darwin's theory.

The civilizing mission held that Europeans had a duty to spread Christianity, Western education, and their laws. Missionaries founded schools and hospitals, while the idea assumed colonized cultures were inferior.

blocks.title: Common trap
blocks.text: Do not confuse motives with justifications. Economic gain was a motive; the civilizing mission was often a justification presented to the public.

sections.takeaway: Ideologies of racial and cultural superiority made conquest seem acceptable to many Europeans and Americans.

connections.title: Industry creates demand
connections.body: Unit 5 described factories that needed raw cotton and markets. Those needs became motives for empire.
connections.transferQuestion: How did industrialization create motives for imperialism?
